question: Walnut anthracnose is a serious problem affecting farmers in Greece. Nurseries where insufficient spraying was carried out have been hit particularly hard. Symptoms are equally severe in walnut groves where pruning and irrigation practices have resulted in high levels of relative humidity in tree crowns, encouraging the growth of the fungus during the growing season.

The fungus overwinters in the affected parts of the trees that fall to the ground and action is needed in order to limit primary infection in the next growing season. This includes removing and burning dried leaves or incorporating them into the soil through shallow ploughing, as well as spraying leaves with a copper formulation before or after they fall to the ground.

However, producers in Greece – and especially in the wake of the recent catastrophic floods – cannot afford to use only the authorised plant protection products required, following the instructions for their use to the letter. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1. What measures could be taken to provide financial support to Greek walnut producers who have suffered serious damages? 2.
What instruments can be used to supply the appropriate plant protection products in order to ensure effective treatment of anthracnose and the seamless continuation of walnut growing in Greece?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.1.

2025) As regards the financial support for walnut producers, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan Regulation1 offers Member States different possibilities to help farmers cope with plant diseases, which may include support for investments, support in a form of loans, guarantees and working capital, risk management, cooperation projects and advisory services.
However, it is up to the Member States to plan and implement such measures.

In the Greek CAP Strategic Plan2, support is allocated in the context of the operational programmes implemented by producer organisations and may be used for the sustainable pest and disease control techniques, and climate change adaptation and mitigation, through advisory services and technical assistance, as well as training, including coaching and exchange of best practices.

Member States might also be able to grant further support in accordance with relevant State aid rules3,4. In accordance with Regulation 1107/20095, active substances are approved at Union level and plant protection products are authorised at Member State level. Fungicides based on the approved active substances copper-based, sulfur, neem oil or Bacillus subtilis could fight anthracnose.

Should plant protection products be not yet authorised in Greece for anthracnose in walnuts, the competent authority may, if the relevant conditions are met, use the provisions in the above-mentioned Regulation to grant mutual recognition to plant protection products authorised in other Member States, extend existing authorisations of plant protection products to minor uses, or grant emergency authorisations for a period not exceeding 120 days.
